summary.headline: V-Guard Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14.1% YoY to INR1,755 crore and PAT 23% to INR112 crore, with FY26 EBITDA margin at 8.8%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was strong, with revenue up 14.1% YoY to INR1,755 crore and EBITDA excluding other income up 19.3% to INR171 crore, while FY26 revenue grew 7% and EBITDA rose 2.6% to INR527 crore. Growth came almost entirely in the second half after a weak summer in the first half. Management is pursuing price hikes of roughly 13% to offset input cost inflation linked to the West Asia conflict, with about 75% landed so far. Net cash rose to INR231 crore and the board recommended a final dividend of INR1.5 per share.

segments.name: Electronics (Stabilizers, UPS, Inverters, Batteries)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 22.3% YoY with all categories growing; about 3% of growth was price and the balance volume, per management. Solar inverters are a newer line, not yet at INR500 crore.

segments.name: Electrical (Wires, Pumps, Switchgears, Modular Switches)
segments.commentary: Largest revenue contributor; Q4 revenue grew 15.9% YoY. Wires face rising competition from new entrants, though management sees the category as low-margin and scale-dependent.

segments.name: Consumer Durables (Fans, Water Heaters, Kitchen Appliances, Air Coolers)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 4.1% YoY; fans and air coolers declined while water heaters and kitchen grew strongly. TPW fans are short of supply due to a plastic raw material shortage.

segments.name: Sunflame (Kitchen Appliances)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 8.6% YoY; the CSD business is still slowing, but non-CSD grew about 16%. GT integration is complete and sales integration is still underway.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for 10-12% volume growth and 1-2% price growth (about 15% total) over time, with higher price growth likely in FY27 due to cost inflation.
EBITDA margin: management says at least 10% is the target for the next year if summer is good, but declined to commit to 11-12%; cited prolonged high cost as a reason for caution.
Expects a good growth year for Consumer Durables on a low base, and a strong start to FY27 given Q4 momentum and a supportive summer forecast.
Cost discipline: no major manpower increases planned; variable pay will fall if top and bottom line targets are missed.
Price increases: about 75% of the required ~13% price hike landed so far; the remaining ~25% is expected as high-cost inventory flows in during May-June.
Raw material supply secured through June for most items; sulfuric acid and certain TPW fan plastics remain tight.
capex_capacity: Management said bulk of new capacity investment is done and ramp-up is under way; capex will still absorb some cash in FY27.
Company spent close to INR300-400 crore over the last 8 years on plants and manufacturing integration.
BLDC is about 40% of ceiling fan sales; BLDC chimneys launched; BLDC mixer grinders not yet launched.
Lighting entry is still work in progress, with launch targeted around early next quarter (Q1 FY27).
No acquisitions planned; any opportunity would be assessed case by case.
demand_pricing: Input costs up 8-13% across representative categories; management says the West Asia conflict has caused commodity inflation and supply shocks, worse than the Ukraine-war period.
Price hikes of about 10-12% (some up to 15-20% industry-wide) face retailer pushback; the company gave case-by-case support in regions where summer has not started.
South India summer demand is strong (sales started early March/April); non-South is mixed due to rain, with East a key market for summer products.
Channel financing covers about 35% of the debtor book (customer-linked, not category-linked); collections were strong in the March quarter.
Kerala is about 15-16% of revenue; no impact seen so far, with summer in Kerala supportive. Non-South contributed 48% of FY26 revenue; South grew 16.2% and non-South 11.8% in Q4.
Competition: wire entrants and lighting peers are entering; management expects consolidation to be slow and sees the top 4-5 brands per category as the survivors.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes have been taken across segments, and is another round needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Input costs up 8-13%; about 75% of the required price increase has landed, with the remaining 25% expected as high-cost inventory arrives in May-June.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Kitchen Appliances segment come out of its slump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes demand is improving, with traction for both V-Guard and Sunflame; Sunflame now uses V-Guard's sales network.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kerala softness affecting demand after March?
qa_highlights.answer: No impact seen so far; Kerala is about 15-16% of revenue and summer there has been supportive. Q1 is primarily a summer quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins reach double digits in one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 FY26 EBITDA was about 9.5%; management is confident of at least 10% once raw material prices normalise, but declined to guide 11-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the solar business size and growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar is below INR500 crore, about 36 months old; management expects it to be among the larger categories in 3-4 years, focused on residential B2C.

qa_highlights.question: Is raw material availability a risk to production?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulfuric acid and polymers are tight; supply is locked up for about a month or more, and management sees no supply challenge through Q1.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation from the West Asia conflict; about 25% of the required price hike is still pending and could face pushback.
Weak non-South summer start; East market is key for summer products and any slip would hurt Q1 FY27 volumes.
Shortage of TPW fan plastic and sulfuric acid could cap output; management expects supply to be about 105 units against 110 demanded.
Rising competition in wires from a large new entrant at the end of 2026 and lighting peers.
Sunflame CSD decline and the pace of benefits from sales integration (expected over the next three quarters); the NPD pipeline lands in H2 FY26 onwards.
Channel inventory is mixed: ceiling fans well stocked after the December 2025 BEE star-rating transition; TPW fans out of stock.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the business and Q4 momentum, but cautious on margins and near-term inflation. Management declined to commit beyond at least 10% EBITDA margin and said it would reassess after a couple of quarters.
key_quotes: We delivered a robust performance in Q4 marked by strong growth in both revenue and profitability.
So far we have navigated these challenges well, which reflects the inherent resilience of the business.
But I wouldn't say 11%, 12%, I would say at least 10% is what we would like to expect there.
We have landed most of the pricing action and I think most companies have announced and taken pricing action.

growth.why: Medium-term aspiration of 10-12% volume plus 1-2% price (~15% total) is held and FY27 EBITDA margin guided to at least 10%, backed by ~75% of a ~13% price hike landed, a strong Q4 (revenue +14.1%) and a good summer start, but no specific capacity or order numbers were given to back the volume targets.
